title: Unbounded cohomology on an acyclic basis of a ringed site
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site, small relative to the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$. Use sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $U\in\mathcal C$, evaluation means sections $M\mapsto M(U)$, with its $\mathcal O(U)$-module structure; $R\Gamma(U,K)$ is evaluation on a K-injective representative of $K$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Write $H^q(K)$ for the cohomology module sheaf, computed as kernel modulo image in degree $q$. Let $\mathcal B\subseteq\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ be a set such that every object has a covering with all members in $\mathcal B$. Let $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ satisfy
$$H^p(R\Gamma(U,H^q(K)[0]))=0\qquad(p>0,\ q\in\mathbf Z,\ U\in\mathcal B).$$
Then there are canonical $\mathcal O(U)$-linear isomorphisms
$$H^q(R\Gamma(U,K))\cong\Gamma(U,H^q(K))\qquad(q\in\mathbf Z,\ U\in\mathcal B).$$
They are natural in $K$ among objects satisfying the displayed vanishing and commute with restriction along every morphism $V\to U$ between objects of $\mathcal B$. They are the edge comparisons induced by the canonical cohomological truncations (bounded-below spectral-sequence comparisons and their eventually constant limit), and in degree zero for a sheaf $K=M[0]$ they are the identity on $M(U)$. No boundedness of $K$ or constancy of $\mathcal O$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BKZ, lemma-cohomology-over-U-trivial, including the truncation-limit construction in its proof; used in spaces-perfect.tex Tag 071Q, lemma-derived-quasi-coherent-small-etale-site.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O)$ and $v_U(M)=M(U)$, with values in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O(U))$. Evaluation is additive and left exact: finite sums and kernels of module sheaves are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The source is Grothendieck by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. So is the target: apply the same statement to the one-object, identity-only site with trivial topology and ring $\mathcal O(U)$; its module sheaves are exactly modules over that ring. Choose the functorial, degreewise injective K-injective replacements supplied by that proposition. Termwise evaluation preserves homotopies, since it preserves sums and compositions in the homotopy equation. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] makes evaluation of these models a functor on the unbounded derived category; changing models gives the same functor up to its canonical comparison. Its bounded-below restriction is the functor in [lem-sp-kinjective-computes], and that lemma identifies $H^p(Rv_U(M[0]))$ with $R^pv_U(M)$, including $R^0v_U(M)=M(U)$. Forgetting the action gives exactly the abelian-group-valued derived evaluation used in the two site-limit lemmas below: both evaluate the same module K-injective model.

source.place: 0BKZ proof, bounded-below derived-evaluation interpretation before applying the spectral sequence; 0D6K, lemma-RGamma-commutes-with-Rlim, uses the underlying abelian evaluation.

proof.text:
For $n\geq0$ put $K_n=\tau_{\geq-n}K$, with maps $c_n:K\to K_n$ and $t_n:K_{n+1}\to K_n$. By [def-kun-truncations], $K_n$ has a bounded-below representative, $H^r(K_n)=0$ for $r<-n$ and $H^r(K_n)=H^r(K)$ canonically for $r\geq-n$. Fix $U\in\mathcal B$. Apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] with $v=v_U$, source and target as verified in step 1, and lower bound $-n$. Its convergent spectral sequence and finite abutment filtration give
$$E_2^{p,r}(n,U)=R^pv_U(H^r(K_n))\Longrightarrow H^{p+r}(R\Gamma(U,K_n)).$$
Step 1 and the hypothesis imply that all columns $p>0$ vanish; columns $p<0$ vanish by the theorem. This applies also to the zero cohomology sheaves below $-n$. No spectral sequence for an unbounded-below complex has been invoked.

source.place: 0BKZ proof, bounded-below spectral-sequence sentence; derived.tex Tag 015J, lemma-two-ss-complex-functor.

proof.text:
Every differential into or out of column zero is zero: for $s\geq2$ its other endpoint has column $-s$ or $s$. Hence $E_\infty^{0,r}=E_2^{0,r}$. All positive graded pieces of the finite filtration on $H^r(R\Gamma(U,K_n))$ vanish. Since $F^0$ is the whole group and the filtration ends in zero, $F^1=0$. The abutment isomorphism in [thm-sp-truncation-e2] therefore gives the column-zero edge
$$e_{n,r,U}:H^r(R\Gamma(U,K_n))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^r(K_n)(U).$$
It is $\mathcal O(U)$-linear: the exact couple, its kernels, images, quotients and the abutment isomorphism are taken in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O(U))$. The construction is functorial for maps of bounded-below complexes: the truncation inclusions, cohomology projections and derived evaluations commute with such a map, so all maps of the exact couples, their successive kernels and quotients, and the finite filtration commute. In particular
$$e_{n,r,U}H^r(R\Gamma(U,t_n))=H^r(t_n)(U)e_{n+1,r,U}.$$
The same reasoning applies to a natural transformation of evaluations on the fixed K-injective models, since it commutes with every differential and truncation map.

source.place: 0BKZ proof, collapse of the bounded-below spectral sequence; functoriality of the truncation exact couple.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-kun-site-truncation-derived-limit] with $E=K$ and $d=0$. Its site is the given small ringed site; its covering subset is exactly $\mathcal B$. Its required vanishing concerns $p>0$ and cohomology sheaves in degrees $r<0$, which is a subset of the vanishing assumed here. Step 1 identifies its abelian-valued evaluation with the underlying evaluation in our hypothesis. Consequently $P=\prod_nK_n$ exists in $D(\mathcal A)$ and
$$K\xrightarrow{(c_n)}P\xrightarrow{1-s}P\longrightarrow K[1],\qquad\operatorname{pr}_ns=t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1},$$
is a derived-limit triangle with the specified canonical projections. This uses a bound only for the cohomology sheaves of $K$, not a cohomological-dimension bound for every sheaf on the site.

source.place: 0BKZ proof, first sentence, applying 0D6P, lemma-is-limit-dimension, with d=0.

proof.text: For the fixed $U$, [lem-kun-site-rgamma-derived-limit] sends the triangle of step 4 to a derived-limit triangle $R\Gamma(U,K)\xrightarrow{p'}\prod_nR\Gamma(U,K_n)\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nR\Gamma(U,K_n)\to R\Gamma(U,K)[1]$ for the tower $(R\Gamma(U,K_n),R\Gamma(U,t_n))_n$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab})$, with $\operatorname{pr}_np'=R\Gamma(U,c_n)$. Since consecutive maps of a distinguished triangle compose to zero, $(1-s)p'=0$, i.e. $R\Gamma(U,c_n)=R\Gamma(U,t_n)R\Gamma(U,c_{n+1})$; hence the maps $H^r(R\Gamma(U,c_n))$ form a cone over the tower $A^r_n=H^r(R\Gamma(U,K_n))$ and define $\rho:H^r(R\Gamma(U,K))\to\varprojlim_nA^r_n$ with $n$th component $H^r(R\Gamma(U,c_n))$. By [lem-pc-milnor-projection-factorization], applied to this Roos triangle, $\rho$ is surjective. By [lem-pc-milnor-boundary-factorization] there is an injection $a:R^1\varprojlim_nA^{r-1}_n\to H^r(R\Gamma(U,K))$ whose image is the kernel of $H^r(R\Gamma(U,K))\to\prod_nA^r_n$, the map with components $H^r(R\Gamma(U,c_n))$; this map is $\rho$ followed by the injective inclusion $\varprojlim_nA^r_n\subseteq\prod_nA^r_n$, so $\ker\rho=a(R^1\varprojlim_nA^{r-1}_n)$. Thus $$0\longrightarrow R^1\varprojlim_n H^{r-1}(R\Gamma(U,K_n))\xrightarrow{a}H^r(R\Gamma(U,K))\xrightarrow{\rho}\varprojlim_n H^r(R\Gamma(U,K_n))\longrightarrow0$$ is exact, and $\rho$ is the map induced by the projections. These statements are about an arbitrary small ringed site and abelian groups, so no constancy of $\mathcal O$, exactness of products of module sheaves, or quasi-compactness hypothesis is inserted.

source.place: 0BKZ displayed exact sequence; 0BKX, equation-ses-Rlim-over-U, from 0D6K, lemma-RGamma-commutes-with-Rlim.

proof.text:
Choose $N\geq\max(0,1-r)$. For $n\geq N$ and $j=r-1,r$, [def-kun-truncations] identifies $H^j(K_n)$ with $H^j(K)$, and $H^j(t_n)$ with its identity: both truncation projections from $K$ give the same quotient in this degree. Step 3 therefore identifies the tails of $A_n^j=H^j(R\Gamma(U,K_n))$ with the constant system $H^j(K)(U)$.
Here is the needed limit calculation, including the finite initial segment. By [lem-pc-derived-limit-roos-abelian-groups], the limit and first derived limit of $(A_n,f_n)$ are the kernel and cokernel of $(x_n)\mapsto(x_n-f_nx_{n+1})$ on $\prod_nA_n$. When $f_n$ is invertible for $n\geq N$, a prescribed $(b_n)$ has a preimage: set $x_N=0$, recursively set $x_{n+1}=f_n^{-1}(x_n-b_n)$ for $n\geq N$, and then set $x_n=b_n+f_nx_{n+1}$ backwards for $n<N$. Thus the cokernel is zero. In the kernel, $x_N$ determines all coordinates, forwards by inverse transitions and backwards by transitions. Projection to $A_N$ is therefore an isomorphism. This proves $R^1\varprojlim A_n^{r-1}=0$ and $\varprojlim A_n^r\cong H^r(K)(U)$, with the latter identification given by any tail coordinate followed by its edge map.

source.place: 0BKZ proof, final two sentences; the explicit kernel/cokernel formula of more-algebra.tex Tag 07KW, lemma-compute-Rlim.

proof.text:
The exact sequence of step 5 and the calculation in step 6 show that $H^r(R\Gamma(U,c_N))$ is a bijection. Define
$$e_{r,U}(K)=e_{N,r,U}\circ H^r(R\Gamma(U,c_N)),\qquad N\geq\max(0,1-r),$$
using the canonical $H^r(K_N)=H^r(K)$. This is an $\mathcal O(U)$-linear isomorphism: the first map is linear by step 3, and the second is evaluation of a morphism of module complexes followed by cohomology. A bijective module homomorphism has a linear inverse, as follows by applying injectivity to $f(ax)=af(x)$. Increasing $N$ leaves this composite unchanged, because $c_N=t_Nc_{N+1}$ and the edge-transition equality of step 3 has identity on $H^r(K)$. Any two admissible choices compare through their maximum. Thus this is exactly the eventually constant limit of the canonical bounded-below truncation edges, without a choice of inverse-limit cone entering its definition.

source.place: 0BKZ proof, passage from the displayed exact sequence to the eventually constant value; explicit canonical edge comparison.

proof.text:
For a morphism $a:K\to L$ between objects satisfying the vanishing, choose the same $N\geq\max(0,1-r)$. Naturality of good truncation gives $c_N^L a=(\tau_{\geq-N}a)c_N^K$. The exact-couple construction of step 3 gives
$$e_{N,r,U}(L)H^r(R\Gamma(U,\tau_{\geq-N}a))=H^r(a)(U)e_{N,r,U}(K).$$
Composing with the projection from $K$ proves naturality of $e_{r,U}$. This applies to derived morphisms: [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents them by maps between K-injective models, uniquely up to homotopy, and evaluation preserves that homotopy as in step 1.
For $h:V\to U$ with $U,V\in\mathcal B$, use the same module K-injective model $I$ to compute both evaluations. Termwise restriction $I(U)\to I(V)$ commutes with differentials, all module chain maps and homotopies, and satisfies $h^*(ax)=h^*(a)h^*(x)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. It gives a natural transformation of the evaluated truncation diagrams. Kernels, images, quotients and induced maps in their exact couples commute with this transformation, so the bounded edge square of step 3 commutes with restriction. The square for $c_N$ also commutes, by termwise restriction of the map representing $c_N$. Compose these two squares to get
$$e_{r,V}(K)\,h^*=h^*\,e_{r,U}(K).$$
This is the required semilinear restriction compatibility, not an assertion of $\mathcal O(U)$-linearity over an unchanged coefficient ring.

source.place: 0BKZ canonical truncation-limit construction; compatibility of the defining maps with complex maps and restriction maps.

proof.text: Finally take $K=M[0]$ satisfying the hypothesis, and degree $r=0$. Its lower truncations $K_n$ are canonically $M[0]$, and the projections $c_n$ are identities. The degree-zero edge is $R^0v_U(M)=v_U(M)$ of [lem-sp-kinjective-computes]. Explicitly, for an injective resolution $0\to M\to I^0\to I^1\to\cdots$, left exactness identifies $M(U)$ with $\ker(I^0(U)\to I^1(U))$ via the augmentation, and the edge is its inverse onto $M(U)$. Thus under the canonical degree-zero identification $e_{0,U}(M[0])$ is the identity on $M(U)$. All constructions above used arbitrary integer $r$, the given covering basis, and arbitrary commutative $\mathcal O$, which proves every clause without a boundedness assumption on $K$.
